Definition: from G4012 and G906; to throw all around, i.e. invest (with a palisade or with clothing):--array, cast about, clothe(-d me), put on.
BiblicalUsage: Periballo means to throw around, to put on, to array. The angel told Peter to cast his garment about him and follow, and the soldiers put a purple robe on Jesus and crowned Him with thorns.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the same word covers both garments: Peter's cloak led him out of prison, and the purple robe led Jesus to the cross.
